frequency_question: How often do major central banks/regulators raise the CCyB above 0% outside of immediate post-crisis rebuilding phases?
membership_rule: Includes any jurisdiction adhering to Basel III standards that implemented a positive CCyB rate when financial stability concerns warranted it, excluding the initial implementation period of 2010-2015.

cases.name: Reserve Bank of New Zealand CCyB Increase
US Federal Reserve CCyB Evaluation Period

provenance_note: 5 cases named, 12 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (2.4x)
coverage_note: 12 major observation points across G10 jurisdictions; believed roughly 15-20 in total across all Basel adherents.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller emerging market economies whose institutional frameworks and political economy differ significantly from the US Federal Reserve.
skeleton: Multiple advanced economies over multiple distinct macroprudential review cycles
multiplier: 4 jurisdictions actively managing the buffer across roughly 3 distinct economic phases over a decade yields approximately 12 distinct policy evaluation opportunities where the baseline was 0% and economic conditions permitted a hike.
validity_reason: The regulatory architecture of Basel III and the structural inertia of central bank macroprudential committees change slowly over multi-year horizons.
